extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journalists, and readers interested in survey methods and the study's methodology (news-industry researchers, media analysts)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of methods and standards used in a mixed-mode national survey of U.S. Millennials (ages 18–34), including sampling, weighting, qualitative group interviews, and analytic reporting conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-mode data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The study used multiple modes of data collection: telephone screening/recruitment followed by an online administration of the main questionnaire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone component completed only by cell phone numbers (no landlines); recruitment involved agreeing to receive an invitation for the web survey by email or text message and providing contact info. Dates: January 5–February 2, 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone recruitment frame (cell phones only; RDD + age-targeted list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Telephone recruitment used cell-phone-only sampling, including random-digit-dial (RDD) and an age-targeted list sample drawn from all 50 states and DC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RDD sample provided by Marketing Systems Group; age-targeted list provided by Scientific Telephone Samples. Targeted sample pulled from multiple commercial consumer databases and demographic data to focus on adults 18–34.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report recruitment funnel and response counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the numbers at each stage of recruitment and eligibility screening (e.g., number providing age info, number eligible, number completing recruitment phase, number completing web survey).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from study: 6,635 adults provided age info; 2,297 were eligible (18–34); 1,759 completed recruitment phase; 1,045 completed the web survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report final response rate using standard method
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute and report the final response rate using an established standard (American Association for Public Opinion Research Response Rate 3 method).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This study reported a final response rate of 14% (AAPOR RR3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and report participant incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer and disclose monetary or other incentives used to compensate participants for different parts of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents were offered one small monetary incentive for the telephone portion and another small incentive for the web portion (compensation for phone usage charges and for completing the web survey).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language accommodations in data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct interviews in respondents' preferred language where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews were conducted in both English and Spanish depending on respondent preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use professional, trained interviewers for recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Telephone recruitments should be completed by professional interviewers who are carefully trained on the specific survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All telephone recruitments in this study were completed by professional interviewers trained for the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling frame design with supplemental targeted sample
rubrics_metrics.description: Design sampling frames that combine a standard RDD frame with a supplemental targeted sample to achieve representativeness for a subpopulation (here, adults 18–34).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sampling frame utilized the standard cell-phone RDD frame with a supplemental cell-phone list sample targeted at 18–34 adults drawn from commercial consumer databases to increase efficiency and coverage of the target demographic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust sampling weights for design and nonresponse
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate and apply sampling weights to adjust for unequal probabilities of selection, nonresponse bias across demographic groups, and coverage issues (e.g., households without cell phones).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling weights were adjusted for the targeted sample bias and calculated for unequal selection probabilities and nonresponse; post-stratification variables included age, sex, race/ethnicity, region, and education. Weighted data were used for all analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report margin of error including design effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the overall margin of error for the weighted estimates and explicitly include the design effect from complex sample design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study reported an overall margin of error of +/- 3.8 percentage points, including the design effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate statistical software and correct SE adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct analyses using software that allows adjustment of standard errors for complex sample designs and report the software used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All analyses were conducted using STATA (version 13), which permits adjustment of standard errors for complex sample designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance conventions and conservative reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report subgroup differences at a specified significance level and apply additional rules (e.g., only report bivariate differences that remain robust in multivariate models controlling covariates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differences between subgroups are reported at the 95% level of statistical significance; bivariate differences are only reported when they also remain robust in a multivariate model controlling for demographic, political, and socioeconomic covariates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative group interview design (semi-structured group interviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct semi-structured group interviews with clear documentation of locations, dates, sample sizes, and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This study conducted 10 semi-structured group interviews in four cities with 23 total participants (17 aged 18–24 and 6 aged 25–34), videotaped with consent, led by a moderator with additional researchers asking probes, using a moderator guide but aiming for casual conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative recruitment approaches (friend groups and intercepts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use targeted recruitment strategies for group interviews such as pre-recruiting friend groups or intercept recruiting on-site, and document the approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chicago and Bay Area groups used pre-recruited friend groups via outside recruiters; Fredericksburg groups were recruited via intercept at a university student center. Recruitment aimed to achieve mixes of demographics and specified tech-savviness criteria in some sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up qualitative activities and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain consent for and conduct optional follow-up qualitative activities (e.g., self-reflection exercises, essays, data diaries) to gather richer information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select participants consented to follow-up activities (self-reflection/interview/essay and a data diary); all participants received monetary incentives for discussion and additional incentive for follow-up completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document location- and context-specific recruitment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: When recruiting across sites, document any site-specific criteria or emphases (e.g., always-online/tech-savvy vs. not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In San Francisco, an emphasis was placed on recruiting respondents who identified as always online and extremely tech-savvy; Oakland groups targeted respondents who were not always online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency, data sharing, and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to publicizing study results and making datasets and study documentation available to scholars and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AP-NORC Center pledged to publicize results and make all datasets and study documentation available; a comprehensive listing of study questions and topline tabulations is available on the project website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational standards to preserve scientific integrity and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to founding principles that mandate preserving scientific integrity and objectivity of research partners and journalistic independence of media partners, with advisory committee review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All work is subject to review by an advisory committee to help ensure standards are met; the Center's mandate includes preventing real or perceived bias in the research and publicizing results.
